Support ticket flowchart

From the customer report to the closed ticket, with escalation to the second line and the case where the customer says the problem is still there.

Open this flow in the editor Free, no sign-up. Opens as a new diagram in your browser.
The flow: Support ticket
Interactive diagram: drag to pan, scroll to zoom. Changes made here are not saved.

How to read the flow

  1. The customer reports a problem; the first line logs the ticket and sets the priority.
  2. If it is a known issue with a documented fix, the first line applies it and replies.
  3. If it is not, the second line investigates the cause.
  4. When a code change is needed, the fix ships in the next release; when it is not, the second line gives the first line a workaround.
  5. Either way, it is the first line that replies to the customer.
  6. The customer confirms whether it is solved. If not, the ticket is reopened and goes back to triage.

The text behind the diagram

This is what Diagramico exports under Export → AI text. It also works the other way round: paste this text into Diagrams → Import text and the diagram is drawn.

DIAGRAM: Support ticket

LANES:
CU = Customer (person)
FL = First line (team)
SL = Second line (team)

NODES:
CU1 start: Reports a problem
FL1 step: Logs the ticket and sets the priority
FL2 decision: Known issue with a documented fix?
FL3 step: Applies the fix and replies to the customer
SL1 step: Investigates the cause
SL2 decision: Needs a code change?
SL3 step: Ships the fix in the next release
SL4 step: Gives the first line a workaround
CU2 decision: Problem solved?
FL4 end: Ticket closed

FLOW:
CU1 > FL1 > FL2
FL2 > FL3 [yes]
FL2 > SL1 [no]
SL1 > SL2
SL2 > SL3 [yes]
SL2 > SL4 [no]
SL3 > FL3
SL4 > FL3
FL3 > CU2
CU2 > FL4 [yes]
CU2 > FL1 [no, reopened]

Ask an AI

Each button copies the request together with the flow text. Paste it into the assistant you use.

Documentation

Write the documentation of this process for the people who will run it: purpose, who takes part, numbered steps by owner and what happens at each decision. Use only what is in the flow and point out anything that is not defined.

Test cases

List the test cases for this process as a table: scenario, starting condition, steps and expected result. Cover every branch of every decision, including the ones that loop back.

Review the logic

Review the logic of this process. Point out decisions with no way out, loops that may never end, steps with no clear owner and cases the flow does not handle. Do not rewrite the process: list the problems by severity.

Adapt it to your case

  • Add a wait step with the response time for each priority (your SLA).
  • If the customer never answers, a branch is missing: close the ticket after how many days?
  • Use comments (key M) to mark the points where the team does not agree yet.
